title: Council rejects permit-only fireworks by-law
subtitle: Changes to hours, fines and dates instead; committee chairs appointed, Connecting Links grant endorsed, budget town halls announced.
overview: Council voted down staff's proposal for a new permit-based fireworks by-law, which would have ended personal use of fireworks {{vote:m9}}. Instead, councillors made a series of changes to the existing by-law: shorter permitted hours, safety information at point of sale, minimum safe distances, higher set fines, fewer discharge days around Victoria Day and Canada Day, and a new seven-day sales window before Diwali. Staff will draft the revised by-law and bring it back at the end of a future council meeting, without further delegations.

Council also endorsed a Connecting Links grant application for the York Road Phase 4 Stage 1 project {{vote:m6}}, and adopted the consent report, which directs staff to create optional guidelines for residential security cameras. Councillors named chairs and vice-chairs for the 2024-2026 term, and a new trustee was appointed to The Elliott Community Board of Trustees.

After the closed session, the mayor reported that staff received direction on two Ontario Land Tribunal matters and on an expression of interest for 170 Stephanie Drive. Budget town halls run November 4 to 8.

decisions.detail: Council defeated the staff proposal, as amended, to replace the 1993 fireworks by-law with a permit-based by-law {{vote:m9}}.
Permitted fireworks hours were shortened so they end at 11 p.m. instead of 11:59 p.m. {{vote:m11}}.
Staff will require point-of-sale employees to give purchasers fireworks safety information and Guelph's rules and guidelines {{vote:m12}}.
Minimum safe distances from residences and vulnerable occupancies such as schools and care facilities will be added to the by-law, with staff to set the distances {{vote:m13}}.
Staff will seek approval from the Regional Senior Justice for new set fines that reflect the impact of violations on the public {{vote:m15}}.
The day before Victoria Day and the day before Canada Day will be removed as permitted discharge days {{vote:m18}}.
Fireworks sales will be restricted to the seven days before Victoria Day, Canada Day and Diwali, which adds a sales window for Diwali {{vote:m19}}.
Council endorsed the city's Connecting Links Intake 10 application to the Ministry of Transportation for the York Road Phase 4 Stage 1 project {{vote:m6}}.

debate: Delegates supporting tighter rules, including the Guelph Humane Society, said fireworks frighten pets, cause lost animals and disturb wildlife such as birds. Others raised noise, PTSD and environmental effects.

Industry and community delegates opposed a ban, saying it would drive sales to neighbouring towns or online and make enforcement harder, citing Brampton. They urged education, point-of-sale training and heavier fines for misuse, and described fireworks as central to Diwali and neighbourhood celebrations.

Councillors backing the staff proposal said fireworks are explosives that trained, insured people should handle, and pointed to drone and laser shows as alternatives. The fire chief described a child being seriously burned by a sparkler.

Councillors opposing it said the problem is not large compared with other issues, that a permit system would be hard to enforce, and that permitted professional displays can be louder. They preferred education, enforcement, distances, shorter hours and higher fines.

Staff said the proposed 300-metre setback was only an example and that they would set a distance allowing backyard use. They also said the by-law currently allows sales only before Victoria Day and Canada Day, so a Diwali sales window needed a separate motion.
